newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares advance in early bourse dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares advance in early bourse dealings.

text.p: German shares were firmer in early bourse dealings on Tuesday as the DAX index initially climbed above 3,800 points in a recovery from Monday's losses.
The 30-share DAX index was up 16.43 points at 3,802.20 points, while the IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was up 34.41 points at 3,801.30 points.
A rising dollar, which was trading above 1.74 marks in morning European dealings, was the main factor driving the market amid a focus on chemical and carmaker shares.
Chemical group Hoechst AG surged about four percent in bourse dealings, rising 3.02 marks to 77 marks after banking group CSFB raised its rating on Hoechst to buy from hold.
CSFB also said Hoechst's shares have a near-term target of 90 marks, which benefited other chemical shares.

BASF AG was up 1.15 marks at 65.60 marks, while Bayer AG was up 1.93 marks at 68.95 marks. Bayer earlier on Tuesday reported that a cancer-causing chemical had been spilled at one of its German plants but that no one was injured.
Most carmakers also benefitted from the dollar, which makes their exports into the United States more competitive.
Luxury carmaker Porsche AG kept up its recent strong gains, rising 250 marks to 2,570 marks and outpacing the DAX advance.
BMW AG was steady at 1,443 marks but Volkswagen AG was down eight marks at 1,329 marks. Daimler-Benz AG, maker of Mercedes vehicles, was up 20 pfennigs at 141.70 marks.

Market attention also focussed on software group Beta Systems AG, the share price of which more than doubled on Monday from its initial public offering price of 100 marks to end the session at 206 marks.
Beta Systems shares were down 18 marks at 188 marks in moderate volumes.
